title: CompactSplat: Spatially Adaptive Gaussian Distribution for Feedforward Scene Reconstruction
claim: Ours reconstructs a scene faithfully with adaptively allocated, far fewer primitives, and fidelity can be traded for memory at inference.
layout: 2 rows split by dashed line; reference, ours and baselines on top, sparsity sweep below
description: The top row has three groups. On the left, titled Reference, are two stacked photos of a bedroom. In the middle, titled CompactSplat, is a Gaussian primitive visualization with a highlighted orange box, next to its rendered novel view. On the right, titled Comparison, is a 2x2 grid of baseline renders (pixelSplat, MVSplat, DepthSplat, YoNoSplat) that show blur, floaters and artifacts, with small red markers on the bed. A dashed gray line separates the bottom section, titled Inference-time Controllable Primitive Number. It has five columns. Each column shows the Gaussian visualization with progressively denser, smaller primitives, and below it an orange-framed zoomed quadtree-like partition grid of the highlighted region. Large primitives cover flat areas and fine cells cover detailed areas. The eye goes first to the large bedroom visuals.
caption: CompactSplat is a highly efficient feed-forward network that predicts 3D scene representations from sparse input images. While previous methods typically allocate one or more Gaussians per pixel—leading to excessive primitives and spatially redundant representations, CompactSplat adaptively allocates primitives based on regional complexity. It concentrates dense Gaussians in texturally rich areas while deploying expanded, scale-modulated primitives in flat regions. This paradigm enables high-fidelity reconstruction with substantially fewer primitives. Crucially, it inherently supports dynamic sparsity control at inference time, allowing seamless trade-offs between visual fidelity and memory footprint across diverse deployment constraints.
abstract: Reconstructing 3D scenes from sparse views without per-scene optimization remains highly challenging, especially for recovering accurate geometry and fine textures. While recent feedforward approaches leverage generalizable 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) for scene generation, they typically assign one or multiple Gaussians to each pixel. Such uniform allocation not only produces highly redundant representations by wasting primitives in homogeneous areas, but also fails to exploit the inherent geometric priors of planar surfaces, often resulting in sub-optimal structural modeling. To address these limitations, we present CompactSplat, a novel feedforward framework that enables a content-aware allocation of 3D Gaussians. By integrating texture-guided spatial partitioning with hierarchical sampling, CompactSplat adaptively distributes primitives - concentrating dense Gaussians in complex regions while tiling flat areas with expanded, scale-modulated primitives. Moreover, our framework inherently supports dynamic sparsity control at inference time, enabling seamless trade-offs between rendering fidelity and memory footprint without requiring network retraining. Extensive experiments on RealEstate10K, DL3DV, and ScanNet demonstrate that CompactSplat consistently outperforms prior methods on both standard metrics and high-resolution rendering consistency, achieving high-fidelity reconstructions with significantly fewer primitives.
